invocations.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a landscape HAVENLINE customer service counter reference board: exactly FOUR large, clean, equally sized panels in a 2 by 2 grid on one continuous neutral light-gray studio background, softly lit with grounded contact shadows. Small centered heading: "HAVENLINE / CUSTOMER COUNTER". Short dark-gray captions under each panel only.

Input image 1 is the authoritative counter identity and construction reference. Re-render that SAME counter, retaining its thick rounded rectangular timber plank top, four stout square timber legs, lower timber shelf and supporting rails, and one compact dark charcoal register fixed at ONE end of the tabletop. Do not redesign it into a shop kiosk or processing machine.
Input image 2 is STYLE ONLY: match its polished, mature stylized 3D finish, gently rounded edges, restrained tactile material detail, soft clean lighting and light gray studio. Do not include the person, clothing or human anatomy.

The counter's warm chestnut/honey timber should have finished softly rounded bevels, subtle natural wood grain, convincing plank joins and coherent construction. The charcoal register has a blue-gray screen, pale distinct keypad buttons, a sloping staff-facing control surface and a plain rounded customer-facing back. Use the same wood, proportions, supports and register in every panel. Clear tabletop, no stock or extra props, no snow.

Rigid construction and handedness:
Define the customer-facing long edge as FRONT, the opposite long edge as STAFF REAR. The register is permanently anchored to the physical LEFT END as seen from the customer front. Its screen and keypad always face the STAFF REAR long edge; it NEVER rotates independently and NEVER changes ends.
TOP LEFT: customer FRONT 0 degrees, exact frontal azimuth with modest elevation: full long face, register at viewer LEFT, plain BACK of register toward camera.
TOP RIGHT: RIGHT END 90 degrees, exact narrow end view with the same modest elevation: view down the full tabletop length from the end OPPOSITE the register, so register is at the FAR end; the staff-facing keypad is seen only in side profile.
BOTTOM LEFT: STAFF REAR 180 degrees, exact rear azimuth with modest elevation: full long face, register at viewer RIGHT, screen and keypad clearly face camera.
BOTTOM RIGHT: LEFT END 270 degrees, opposite exact narrow end view with same modest elevation: view from the register end so register is NEAREST camera; staff-facing keypad is in the opposite side profile from the 90-degree panel.

Captions exactly:
"CUSTOMER FRONT 0°"
"RIGHT END 90°"
"STAFF REAR 180°"
"LEFT END 270°"

Each panel is one complete full counter at generous readable scale. Perspective must correspond to the actual four cardinal camera directions, not four three-quarter views. All four legs, lower shelf and joints exist consistently even where correctly occluded. All feet rest on the same studio floor. Keep the whole counter and register inside each panel. No humans, arrows, diagram lines, measurements, prices, logos, machinery, duplicated registers, floating pieces, dramatic vignette, navy backgrounds or busy decorative borders. This is a static studio reference sheet, not a gameplay screenshot.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Create the DIAGONAL companion board for the approved HAVENLINE customer service counter in input image 1. Use exactly the same polished stylized 3D counter, materials, register, leg/shelf construction, neutral light-gray studio, soft lighting, delicate panel borders and typography. Exactly FOUR equal large panels in a clean landscape 2 by 2 grid, whole objects fully visible and grounded. Small heading "HAVENLINE / CUSTOMER COUNTER". Do not copy the cardinal camera angles.

Input image 1 is the APPROVED exact construction and studio anchor: one thick rounded warm timber plank tabletop, four stout square timber legs, coherent lower timber shelf/support rails and a compact dark register at one end.
Input image 2 is the original same-counter identity reference only; its navy background and original typography are not the requested presentation.
Input image 3 is the latest user STYLE authority only, for mature polished stylized3D materials and light-gray studio. Do not include any person or clothing.

Generate four true three-quarter views at the exact distinct horizontal azimuths below, keeping the same modest camera elevation, object scale and projection. Rotate the camera around ONE rigid counter; never flip the image or relocate parts:
TOP LEFT: FRONT-RIGHT45°, showing customer front and opposite/right end.
TOP RIGHT: REAR-RIGHT135°, showing staff rear and opposite/right end.
BOTTOM LEFT: REAR-LEFT225°, showing staff rear and register/left end.
BOTTOM RIGHT: FRONT-LEFT315°, showing customer front and register/left end.

The register remains physically fixed at the counter's LEFT end as seen from CUSTOMER FRONT0° in image1. Its plain back faces the customer side, and its blue-gray screen and pale keypad always face the STAFF REAR side. In front obliques45/315, the plain back dominates; in rear obliques135/225 the controls are clearly visible. From right-end obliques45/135 the register is at the farther physical end; from left-end obliques225/315 it is nearer. Every leg, plank, shelf, rail, bevel and register key layout belongs to the exact SAME object.

Captions exactly:
"FRONT-RIGHT 45°"
"REAR-RIGHT 135°"
"REAR-LEFT 225°"
"FRONT-LEFT 315°"

Keep the tabletop empty except for its one anchored register. The long lower shelf is a coherent supported surface between the same four legs; no X braces or extra cabinet panels. Clean subtle wood grain, soft rounded join edges, warm honey/chestnut color and charcoal register match image1 exactly. No humans, stock, snow, extra machinery, duplicate registers, dramatic shadows, navy backdrop, geometry swaps, arbitrary attachments, dimension arrows or extra text. This is a static reference board, not a gameplay scene.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Create the FOUR-PANEL DETAIL companion board for the exact approved HAVENLINE customer service counter in input image1. Match that same counter and studio style exactly. Landscape2 by2 layout, thin quiet panel outlines, neutral light-gray background, soft grounded studio shadows and legible dark-gray short captions. Small heading "HAVENLINE / CUSTOMER COUNTER". This board clarifies construction and repeated placement; it contains no people.

Input image1 is the APPROVED construction and studio anchor. Preserve its thick rounded honey/chestnut plank top, four square legs, lower timber shelf/support rails and ONE dark charcoal end-mounted register.
Input image2 is the original same-counter construction identity reference; do not use its navy background or typography.
Input image3 is the newest user STYLE authority for polished mature stylized3D material quality and gray studio only; no person, clothing, head, hands or dummy.

Critical rigid identity: register fixed at the LEFT physical end when viewing the customer FRONT. Register screen/keypad always face the STAFF REAR long side. Nothing changes size, design, leg count, shelf height, tabletop depth, material or register end across panels.

TOP LEFT, caption "STAFF REGISTER": a large readable rear three-quarter closeup of the anchored register AND its nearby tabletop corner. Show the same blue-gray screen, pale distinct keypad buttons, rounded charcoal casing, and stable contact with the timber top. The register remains seated on the tabletop; do not isolate or float it. Controls face the staff side.
TOP RIGHT, caption "STOCK SURFACE": a high elevated rear three-quarter view showing the FULL countertop and generous clear handoff/stock surface beside the end-mounted register. Keep the tabletop empty so its usable surface, plank joins, thickness and bounded edge are clear. Entire counter may be visible below, consistent with image1.
BOTTOM LEFT, caption "SHELF & SUPPORTS": a low rear three-quarter construction close view showing the full lower shelf, its supporting rails and the four square legs meeting the floor. Include enough of the tabletop to establish attachment and leg length. Keep clear separations and plausible join contact; no new X braces, drawers, doors or metal brackets.
BOTTOM RIGHT, caption "TWO COUNTERS": two identical complete instances of this EXACT counter placed next to each other with a visible gap, both facing the same customer direction, seen from front-right45°. Each has exactly its own single register on the same physical end, with backs toward the customer side. Both counters are whole, equally sized, on the same floor and clearly independent. Keep a clean open staff approach behind them, without a surrounding fence or scene.

Use generous readable composition for all four panels. Keep thick rounded timber edges, restrained wood grain and coherent soft shadows, same proportions and register details as image1. No customers or staff, no human silhouettes, food, money, logs, floor pads, prices, machinery, additional counter design, numbers, arrows, callout lines, snow, navy background or decorative border. Do not invent implementation sockets or game mechanics.
